skill.name: streaming-llm-responses
skill.description: Implement real-time streaming UI patterns for AI chat applications. Use this skill to add response lifecycle handlers, progress indicators, client effects, client tools, and thread state synchronization.
skill.summary: Build responsive AI chat interfaces with streaming response events and client-side UI updates.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The static external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and TypeScript template literals in documentation examples. The network finding is also a false positive because it cites an abstract sample helper, not an HTTP client or external destination. Two contextual implementation risks remain: unfiltered client state returned to AI tools and unvalidated server-sent effect payloads.

remediation.issue: Client tool examples return browser state and form values without filtering.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to redact sensitive fields, require user consent for private data, and return only the minimum state needed by the AI.

remediation.issue: Client effect examples trust server-sent payload shapes before updating UI state.
remediation.suggestion: Show schema validation for every effect name and payload before applying state changes, map actions, or notifications.

semantic_findings.title: Unfiltered Client State Returned To AI Tools
semantic_findings.description: The examples return selected item IDs, viewport data, and full form values from browser client tools to the AI without redaction or consent checks. Real implementations could expose sensitive client-side state if developers copy these examples unchanged.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly shows client tools returning browser state and form values. The risk depends on application data sensitivity, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Server-Sent Effect Payloads
semantic_findings.description: The examples apply server-sent effect data directly to UI state, maps, and notifications without schema validation. Malformed or unexpected payloads could corrupt client state or create misleading UI behavior in copied implementations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited handlers directly trust the effect name and data shapes in example code. This is a contextual robustness risk rather than evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Streaming chat interfaces can feel slow or inconsistent when response state is not coordinated. This skill provides practical ChatKit patterns for lifecycle events, progress updates, client effects, and thread synchronization.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to wire ChatKit response start, response end, and error handlers.
Provides client effect patterns for UI updates, notifications, map actions, and selection modes.
Explains progress update events for long-running backend operations.
Documents client tool patterns for reading selected items, viewport state, and form data.
Covers thread change and thread load handlers for persistence and loading states.
Includes a reference file with a complete streaming handler configuration.
limitations: The skill provides documentation examples, not a ready-made application.
Examples use placeholder variables such as API_URL and DOMAIN_KEY.
Client data privacy controls must be added by each application team.
It focuses on ChatKit-style streaming patterns and may need adaptation for other SDKs.

use_cases.title: Add Response Lifecycle Feedback
use_cases.description: Use response start, response end, and error handlers to lock UI controls and show loading state during AI responses.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend engineers building AI chat products

use_cases.title: Stream Backend Progress To Users
use_cases.description: Emit progress update events during search, analysis, or processing so users can see work as it happens.

use_cases.title: Synchronize Interactive Client State
use_cases.description: Use client effects and client tools to coordinate maps, canvases, forms, and thread state with an AI conversation.
use_cases.target_user: Product teams building interactive AI workflows

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Streaming State
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for response lifecycle handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add response start, response end, and error handlers to my ChatKit chat component. Keep the UI locked while the assistant is responding.

prompt_templates.title: Show Long Operation Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design progress update events for a backend tool that searches, analyzes results, and returns a final answer to the chat UI.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Client Effects
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan client effects for map markers, notifications, and selection modes. Include validation steps before applying effect data.

prompt_templates.title: Design Full Streaming Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my AI chat architecture for lifecycle events, progress updates, client tools, thread persistence, privacy controls, and error recovery.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to prevent users from editing a map while an AI response is streaming.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends response lifecycle handlers that lock the map on response start, unlock it on response end, and also unlock it in error handling.

output_examples.input: A backend tool performs a slow article search and the UI needs visible progress.
output_examples.output: The skill describes progress messages for search start, result discovery, batch processing, and finalization before returning the answer.

output_examples.input: A team wants the AI to read selected canvas items before making a recommendation.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a client tool pattern and recommends returning only the selected identifiers needed for the decision.

best_practices: Always unlock UI state in both response end and error handlers.
Validate effect names and payload shapes before updating client state.
Return the smallest useful client tool response and redact sensitive fields.
anti_patterns: Do not let users trigger conflicting actions while an AI response is still streaming.
Do not perform heavy synchronous work inside client effect handlers.
Do not send complete form or browser state to the AI when a smaller response is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you implement streaming response feedback, progress indicators, client effects, client tools, and thread state handling for AI chat interfaces.

faq.question: Does this skill include a complete chat application?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns and examples that you adapt inside your own application.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it make external network requests?
faq.answer: The skill files do not implement network calls. The examples assume your ChatKit application already has an API endpoint.

faq.question: What should I review before copying the client tool examples?
faq.answer: Review the data returned from the browser. Redact private values and request consent before sharing sensitive client state with an AI system.

faq.question: How should client effects be handled safely?
faq.answer: Validate each effect name and payload shape before applying UI updates, map actions, notifications, or state changes.
